 The Kabul Tribune (KT) — Afghanistan strengthened their preparations 
for the 2027 Cricket World Cup with a convincing victory over Zimbabwe in the 
final of a triangular series that also featured Bangladesh. 
 Afghanistan produced an impressive performance throughout 
the competition, combining disciplined bowling with confident batting to 
underline their growing strength ahead of next year's international cricket 
schedule and the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup. 
 After Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza elected to bat first, 
Afghanistan's bowlers quickly took control, reducing the opposition to 26-3 in 
the seventh over. Fazalhaq Farooqi and Azmatullah Omarzai struck early before 
Bilal Sami dismissed experienced batter Brendan Taylor for 9. 
 Raza provided the main resistance with 68 runs, while Ryan 
Burl contributed 31 as the pair shared a 60-run partnership to help Zimbabwe 
recover from their early setbacks. 
 However, Burl's dismissal in the 27th over triggered another 
collapse. Mohammad Nabi and Rashid Khan dismantled the lower order as Zimbabwe 
was bowled out for 169. 
 Rashid led the bowling attack with 3-41, while Sami took 
2-27. Farooqi finished with 2-41 and Nabi claimed 2-25. 
 Afghanistan's chase was led by Ibrahim Zadran, who remained 
unbeaten on 70. Rahmanullah Gurbaz provided early support before being 
dismissed for 30, with Afghanistan reaching 68 in the 10th over. 
 Zimbabwe tightened its bowling during the middle overs, 
dismissing Sediqullah Atal for 6, but the low target allowed Afghanistan to 
maintain control of the chase. 
 Captain Rahmat Shah scored 43 and shared a valuable 
partnership with Zadran. Although Wessly Madhevere dismissed Rahmat, 
Afghanistan completed the chase in the 35th over to secure the title. 
 The victory capped an impressive turnaround after Zimbabwe 
won the opening match of the tri-series against Bangladesh by 99 runs. Craig 
Ervine scored 93 and Taylor made 81 in that match. 
 Afghanistan responded with a 158-run victory over Zimbabwe 
before defeating Bangladesh by seven wickets to qualify for the final. Rashid 
played a key role in those wins, taking eight wickets across the two matches. 
 The series also provided opportunities for emerging players, 
including Sami and Allah Mohammad Ghazanfar, as Afghanistan continued to build 
depth in their squad. 
 Afghanistan will next face Zimbabwe in a three-match Twenty20 
international series, followed by a two-match Test series. All five matches are 
scheduled to take place in Sharjah. 
 The T20 series begins on Oct. 27, with further matches on 
Oct. 29 and Nov. 1. The first Test is scheduled for Nov. 5-9, followed by the 
second from Nov. 13-17. 
 The matches will give both teams further opportunities to 
assess their squads and build momentum ahead of future international 
competitions.
